sites.filters: Listing exposes a Salary filter, feature chips and a Bank filter. sites.aedFormatting: Currency shown as a separate AED label adjacent to the value. Tile labels recurring cost as Annual Fee; detail page groups charges under Rates and Fees and separately labels late-payment, over-limit and optional-protection charges. Compact currency-code-plus-value presentation.
sites.languageToggle: English and Arabic are first-class routes; header/footer exposes عربي/English links; Arabic listing uses Arabic labels and localised slugs and is visibly RTL. Some navigation/product text remains untranslated or mixed-language.

sites.compareFlow: Prominent Compare entry point and comparison-oriented results layout; tiles expose a compare affordance; maximum selections not stated; detail page has a compact attribute table and a separate Apply path.
sites.mobilePatterns: Responsive with lazy/infinite loading rather than pagination. No clearly labelled sticky comparison bar or documented mobile table strategy in the markup; detail comparison table is a compact block to test at narrow widths.
sites.trustSignals: Discloses information is illustrative and subject to change, advises a trained professional, includes an implications-of-non-payment notice, identifies UAE Central Bank regulation for insurance. sites.navigation: IA grouped into Insurance, Banking products, Money Saving Tools & Tips and Everything else; Banking includes credit cards alongside loans and accounts; tools include calculators. Footer repeats categories, guides, terms, privacy, about, contact, countries and language routes, plus regulatory/disclaimer content and a WhatsApp contact.
adopt: Salary-transfer, Islamic/Sharia and bank as explicit, scannable filters.

Parallel English/Arabic routes with localised labels and genuine RTL, auditing untranslated leftovers.
Compact comparison summary with a prominent CTA and a deeper eligibility/requirements section.
Regulatory/disclaimer language and non-payment warnings close to the decision context.

Mixed Arabic/English labels in a supposedly localised journey.
Ambiguous comparison limit or selection state; application CTAs obscuring the comparison task.

uaeConventions: AED commonly shown as the explicit three-letter code beside a value rather than a symbol.
Minimum salary, salary transfer and Sharia/Islamic status are high-value UAE decision attributes and work as visible filter/comparison fields.
English/Arabic route switching is expected; Arabic support should include RTL layout, localised navigation and product labels.
UAE comparison UX benefits from prominent eligibility requirements, terms/change disclaimers, non-payment warnings and regulator/licence disclosures.
Large category mega-menus combine comparison products, calculators, guides and legal/help links; the footer is a major trust and navigation surface.
recommendationsForDubaipoints: Filter-first card directory with salary band, salary-transfer requirement, Islamic/Sharia status and issuer filters, filter state preserved in the URL.
Consistent card-tile anatomy: issuer/product, eligibility cue, AED-labelled fee fields, key benefits, compare checkbox, honest editorial CTA; Apply/Visit Bank only in disclosed referral contexts.
Mobile comparison tray showing selected cards with clear selection state; wide tables as stacked sections or horizontally scrollable tables with accessible headings.
English/Arabic switching with a real RTL stylesheet and QA for mixed-language labels, numbers, dates and table alignment.
Last updated, methodology/how-we-earn, affiliate/referral disclosure, eligibility caveats and UAE regulatory context easy to find near results and in the footer.

learnFrom: Small, stable primary navigation repeated in the footer.
